answer: To securely distribute high-value resources, we employ a Proof-of-Computational-Expenditure mechanism that binds identity to real hardware. Harvesting network nectar requires unique processing power, preventing a single "sparrow" from scavenging the virtual "orchard" simultaneously. Attacking this system is economically prohibitive; an interloper must rent numerous distinct physical rigs, thereby dissipating capital that would otherwise fund coordinated fraud.
